samf-senior-2012-r1-04.title: Compare the sums
samf-senior-2012-r1-04.body:
The five numbers add up to $5\cdot 12 = 60$. The remaining four add up to $4\cdot14 = 56$. The removed number is $60-56 = 4$.

**Answer: (B) 4**

samf-senior-2012-r1-05.title: Semicircles
samf-senior-2012-r1-05.body:
The two small circles touch and each touches the large circle, so their centres lie on a diameter of the large circle, whose radius is $2+2 = 4$. The shaded region is the upper half of the large circle with the upper halves of the two small circles removed:
$$\tfrac12\pi\cdot4^2-2\cdot\tfrac12\pi\cdot2^2 = 8\pi-4\pi = 4\pi.$$

**Answer: (E) $4\pi$**

samf-senior-2012-r1-05.title: Whole circles
samf-senior-2012-r1-05.body:
By symmetry the shaded area is half of (large circle minus two small circles): $\frac12(16\pi-4\pi-4\pi) = 4\pi$.

**Answer: (E) $4\pi$**

samf-senior-2012-r1-06.title: Find the side length
samf-senior-2012-r1-06.body:
Each figure is a square. Surrounding it adds one square on every side, so the side grows by 2: the side of figure $n$ is $2n-1$ (1, 3, 5, ...). Figure 10 has side 19, so it contains $19^2 = 361$ unit squares.

**Answer: (D) 361**

samf-senior-2012-r1-06.title: Count the rings
samf-senior-2012-r1-06.body:
Figure 1 has 1 square; each new ring adds the 8, 16, 24, ... squares needed to surround the previous square. Total for figure 10: $1+8(1+2+\cdots+9) = 1+8\cdot45 = 361$.

**Answer: (D) 361**

samf-senior-2012-r1-07.title: Use a 3-4-5 triangle
samf-senior-2012-r1-07.body:
A gradient of $3:4$ means rise : run $= 3:4$, so rise : run : slope length $= 3:4:5$ (Pythagoras). Walking 15 m along the path is $3\cdot5$, so the rise is $3\cdot3 = 9$ m.

**Answer: (C) 9**

samf-senior-2012-r1-08.title: Compare watch time with real time
samf-senior-2012-r1-08.body:
In each real hour the watch advances only 55 minutes. From 07:00 to 09:45 the watch has advanced $2\cdot60+45 = 165 = 3\cdot 55$ minutes, so 3 real hours have passed. The real time is 10:00.

**Answer: (B) 10:00**

samf-senior-2012-r1-08.title: Use a ratio
samf-senior-2012-r1-08.body:
Watch time : real time $= 55:60 = 11:12$. So real time $= 165\cdot\frac{12}{11} = 180$ minutes $=3$ hours.

**Answer: (B) 10:00**

samf-senior-2012-r1-09.title: Find the cycle
samf-senior-2012-r1-09.body:
Cards go to persons $1,4,7,10,3,6,9,2,5,8$, and then it repeats with period 10 (each step moves 3 places round the table, and 3 and 10 have no common factor, so all 10 people are visited before repeating). Card 52 is in the same position as card $52-50 = 2$ of the cycle, i.e. person 4.

**Answer: (B) 4th**

samf-senior-2012-r1-09.title: Formula
samf-senior-2012-r1-09.body:
Card $n$ goes to the person whose number is $1+3(n-1) = 3n-2$, counted round the table. For $n=52$ this is $154$, and $154 = 15\cdot10+4$, so it is person 4.

**Answer: (B) 4th**

samf-senior-2012-r1-11.title: Group in fours
samf-senior-2012-r1-11.body:
Group the terms as $(1+2+3-4)+(5+6+7-8)+\cdots+(97+98+99-100)$. The groups are $2, 10, 18, \ldots, 194$: 25 groups forming an arithmetic sequence. The sum is $\frac{25}{2}(2+194) = 2450$.

**Answer: (D) 2450**

samf-senior-2012-r1-11.title: Correct the signs
samf-senior-2012-r1-11.body:
Without the minus signs the sum would be $1+\cdots+100 = 5050$. Each of the 25 terms $4,8,\ldots,100$ was subtracted instead of added, so subtract twice their sum: $4(1+2+\cdots+25) = 4\cdot325 = 1300$. The result is $5050-2\cdot1300 = 2450$.

**Answer: (D) 2450**

samf-senior-2012-r1-12.title: Count by direction
samf-senior-2012-r1-12.body:
The 12 edges of the box come in three directions (length, breadth, height), with 4 parallel edges in each direction. Four edges give $\binom42 = 6$ pairs, so the total is $3\cdot6 = 18$.

**Answer: (A) 18**

samf-senior-2012-r1-13.title: Think about the motion
samf-senior-2012-r1-13.body:
The ball starts at rest at height $h_0>0$, so the graph starts at a positive height with horizontal tangent; it then speeds up under gravity, so $h$ falls more and more steeply until it reaches 0. Graph (A) has $t$ standing still, (B) has no motion, (C) is constant speed, (E) has the ball rising. Only (D) fits.

**Answer: (D)**

samf-senior-2012-r1-14.title: Count pairs
samf-senior-2012-r1-14.body:
There are $\binom92 = 36$ pairs. The sum is even when both are even ($\binom52=10$ pairs) or both odd ($\binom42=6$ pairs): $\frac{16}{36} = \frac49$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac49$**

samf-senior-2012-r1-14.title: Sequential probabilities
samf-senior-2012-r1-14.body:
P(both even) $=\frac59\cdot\frac48 = \frac5{18}$; P(both odd) $=\frac49\cdot\frac38 = \frac16$. The sum is $\frac5{18}+\frac3{18} = \frac49$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac49$**

samf-senior-2012-r1-15.title: Convert units
samf-senior-2012-r1-15.body:
$100$ m in $9.69$ s is $\frac{100}{9.69}\approx10.32$ m/s. Multiplying by 3.6 gives about $37.2$ km/h.

**Answer: (D) 37**

samf-senior-2012-r1-15.title: Compare with 10 s
samf-senior-2012-r1-15.body:
100 m in 10 s is $10$ m/s $= 36$ km/h. Since 9.69 s is about 3% less than 10 s, the speed is about 3% more: $36\cdot1.03\approx37$.

**Answer: (D) 37**

samf-senior-2012-r1-16.title: Unroll the cylinder
samf-senior-2012-r1-16.body:
Cut the curved surface along a vertical line and flatten it into a rectangle. $B$ is opposite $A$, so it is half the circumference away horizontally: $\frac12\cdot2\pi\cdot4 = 4\pi$, and 8 below. The shortest path is the straight line on the flattened surface:
$$\sqrt{8^2+(4\pi)^2} = \sqrt{64+16\pi^2} = 4\sqrt{4+\pi^2}.$$

**Answer: (B) $4\sqrt{\pi^2+4}$**

samf-senior-2012-r1-17.title: Inclusion-exclusion
samf-senior-2012-r1-17.body:
Learners taking at least one of the two subjects: $54+48-16 = 86$ (the 16 who take both were counted twice). Adding the 12 who take neither gives $86+12 = 98$.

**Answer: (E) 98**

samf-senior-2012-r1-18.title: Angles at a vertex
samf-senior-2012-r1-18.body:
At each vertex of the square, 360° is shared by the square's $90^\circ$ and two octagon angles of $135^\circ$: $90+135+135 = 360$. For the triangle, the angle $60^\circ$ and two equal polygon angles $\alpha$ must fill $360^\circ$: $\alpha = 150^\circ$.

A regular $n$-gon has interior angle $180^\circ-\frac{360^\circ}{n}$. Setting this to $150^\circ$ gives $\frac{360}{n} = 30$, so $n = 12$.

**Answer: (C) 12**

samf-senior-2012-r1-19.title: Equations
samf-senior-2012-r1-19.body:
Let each link have length $x$ and each overlap $y$. A chain of $n$ links has length $nx-(n-1)y$. Then $2x-y = 12$ and $5x-4y = 27$. From the first, $y = 2x-12$; substituting: $5x-8x+48 = 27$, so $x = 7$, $y = 2$. For 40 links: $40\cdot7-39\cdot2 = 280-78 = 202$.

**Answer: (A) 202**

samf-senior-2012-r1-19.title: Linear growth
samf-senior-2012-r1-19.body:
Going from 2 to 5 links adds 3 links and $27-12 = 15$ cm, so each extra link adds 5 cm. From 2 to 40 links: $12+38\cdot5 = 202$.

**Answer: (A) 202**

samf-senior-2012-r1-20.title: Split into triangles
samf-senior-2012-r1-20.body:
The area is the sum of the areas of triangles $PAB, PBC, PCD, PDA$. With $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_4$ the angles at $P$, the area is $\frac12(2\cdot3\sin\theta_1+3\cdot5\sin\theta_2+5\cdot6\sin\theta_3+6\cdot2\sin\theta_4)$. Since $\sin\theta\le1$, this is at most $\frac12(6+15+30+12) = 31.5$, with equality when all four angles are $90^\circ$ (possible, as the four angles sum to $360^\circ$).

**Answer: (A) 31.5**

samf-senior-2012-r1-20.title: Use the diagonals
samf-senior-2012-r1-20.body:
The area of a quadrilateral is $\frac12 AC\cdot BD\sin\varphi\le\frac12AC\cdot BD$. Now $AC\le AP+PC = 7$ and $BD\le BP+PD = 9$, so the area is at most $\frac12\cdot7\cdot9 = 31.5$. Equality holds when $P$ is on both diagonals and they are perpendicular.

**Answer: (A) 31.5**
